summary: Environment A direct binary verification for the Phase 6.4 Windows rebuild (Operator Ergonomics: buried audio/speech error visibility). The first Phase 6.x slice to touch Rust - this file documents both the new symbols this phase's backend changes produce and the same honest strings-tooling limitation for the frontend-side changes, established in Phase 6.1-6.3's own evidence files.

installer.note: The SHA-256 and file size both changed from the Phase 6.3 baseline, confirming a genuinely new artifact was packaged - not a stale/copied installer.

dllPresenceCheck.method: Extracted the installer with 7z and confirmed all three bundled runtime DLLs are present at the installer root.

newSymbolProof.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings/nm against the extracted cip-desktop.exe, searching for this phase's new LiveStatus fields and pure helper.

result.audioErrorText: 1 occurrence - the new serde camelCase field name, confirming LiveStatus.audio_error_text is genuinely compiled into this exact binary.
result.error_text_if: 0 occurrences via nm - this small, pure, two-call-site function was inlined by the release-mode optimizer, as expected and consistent with this project's established pattern for small pure functions (e.g. classify_overload, rms_level/is_silence, should_reset_segmenter_on_overload were all inlined too) - verified instead via 3 dedicated unit tests, all passing as part of this phase's regression suite.

rustSymbolRegressionCheck.method: Re-checking every prior-phase Rust-side symbol/string this project's manifest already tracks, to confirm zero regression despite this phase's own Rust changes.

result.whisper_full_with_state: 93 occurrences via nm - identical to both the Phase 6.2 and Phase 6.3 baselines, further confirming the auxiliary-symbol count is stable when the vendored C++ source (untouched again this phase) doesn't change.

rustSymbolRegressionCheck.conclusion: Every previously-tracked Rust-side symbol/string count is unchanged, alongside the two new fields and the (expected, inlined) new helper - confirms this phase's Rust changes are additive only, with no regression to any prior phase's compiled surface.

frontendTextSearchLimitation.attempted: Searched the extracted cip-desktop.exe for this phase's new frontend text: 'Last error' (the new audio diagnostics line's leading text, shared with speech's own pre-existing line).
frontendTextSearchLimitation.controlExperiment: Also searched for a frontend-only string known to be present and UNCHANGED by this phase: 'Needs Attention'. ALSO returned 0 matches, reproducing the Phase 6.1/6.2/6.3 finding a fourth time.
frontendTextSearchLimitation.conclusion: Confirms, again, that Tauri's compressed embedded frontend bundle is opaque to plain strings(1)/nm(1) scanning - the same real, already-documented tooling limitation, not a build defect specific to this phase.
correctnessEvidenceUsedInstead: Fresh Vite build produced a new asset bundle hash for this rebuild, distinct from the Phase 6.3 build's bundle.
Full frontend test suite: 242/242 passing (unchanged count - this phase's frontend work is rendering/interpolation of already-typed data, not new pure logic).
Full backend test suite: cip-desktop went from 313 to 316 passing tests (3 new error_text_if cases), under both feature configurations.
Installer SHA-256 and file size both changed from the Phase 6.3 baseline, confirming the newly-built bundle and binary were genuinely packaged into this installer.

architectureVerification.outerInstallerStub: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386, Nullsoft Installer self-extracting archive - standard NSIS bootstrapper, unchanged from every prior phase.
architectureVerification.installedApplicationBinary: cip-desktop.exe: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64, confirmed genuinely x64.

conclusion: This phase's Rust-side changes are directly proven present via two new serde field-name strings, with every prior-phase symbol/string count confirmed unchanged (including whisper_full_with_state's auxiliary count remaining stable at 93 for a third consecutive rebuild). This phase's frontend-side changes rest on the same honest, already-documented strings-tooling limitation as Phase 6.1-6.3, worked around the same way: a fresh build hash, a changed installer SHA-256, and a full passing test suite - never a fabricated string match.
